title: mamori.restoration-scope/1
description: What came back from a model and what became of it, for one scope, carrying no restored value. The return half of mamori.protection-scope/1: join them on `scope`. Together they are the lineage of one round trip -- original to protected to answer to restored -- with nothing sensitive in either record.

contract.description: Frozen contract identifier. A consumer that does not recognise one must refuse the record rather than read the fields it happens to know.

by.description: Producer, as name/version. The version says which placeholder grammar was in force, which is what decides whether a mangled token was recognised at all.

scope.description: The scope whose placeholders were resolved. The same value the protection record carries, and the only thing joining the two halves. A scope is not derived from any document.

clean.description: Whether every placeholder-shaped run in the answer was one this scope had allocated. False means the answer contained something shaped like a placeholder that nobody minted -- a model inventing one, or a response fishing for a value it was never given. A consumer that does not find this property must read it as false.

restored.description: Tokens found in the answer and replaced with their values. The token is admissible for the same reason it is in the protection record: a holder of the protected text recovers it with one regular expression, so this discloses nothing they did not have. The value is never here.

tampered.description: The subset of `restored` whose surface form the model had altered -- `<PERSON _ 001>`, `person_1`, a bracket style changed. Recorded because a rising count is how a model that has started rewriting placeholders is noticed before a restoration silently fails. Always a subset of `restored`, by identity.

unknown.description: Placeholder-shaped runs the answer carried that this scope never allocated, canonicalised to (kind, index). **The surface form is deliberately not here.** A surface is whatever a model typed, and putting it in an audit line puts model output verbatim into somebody's log; the identity is bounded by the placeholder grammar. Nothing was substituted for these -- they are still standing in the restored text where a reader can see them.

unused.description: Tokens allocated in this scope that the answer did not mention. Usually harmless -- the model simply did not need them -- and worth recording because 'the answer used none of them' is the signature of a response about the wrong conversation.

token.description: The canonical placeholder, e.g. <PERSON_001>. Never a surface form and never a value.

$comment: One invariant this schema cannot express and a consumer must enforce: `tampered` is a subset of `restored`. And one reading rule -- a record with `clean: false` says the answer contained a token nobody minted, which is a fact about the answer and not about this library; it is not evidence of an attack and it is the only place such a thing is visible at all. ENCODING: a record is UTF-8, stated here because a contract that does not name its encoding is one its own producer eventually gets wrong -- a sibling wrote its JSON report in the platform locale, could not parse it back, and published a hash over bytes that were not in the file, with nothing violated because nothing had been stated. Decode as UTF-8 and never as the platform default; encode the same way, including to a redirected stream, which is where the locale gets its second chance.
